title: October 2026
monthlyRecap: October combined continued SEO improvements with the addition of Google Ads management. We published three educational articles, completed the prenatal physiotherapy page, strengthened internal linking, and corrected 25 French meta descriptions. We also corrected the French prenatal page title and URL with a permanent redirect, and verified all 50 URLs in the duplicate-description audit.

November 1, 2026 follow-up to October: we reviewed the Google Ads, Google Tag Manager and GA4 setup and confirmed that a Book Online click fired the Jane click tags once in the observed test. A genuine appointment booking was also completed through Jane. The before-and-after booking-import and double-counting checks remain pending; tracking has not been verified as fully fixed.

Reporting note — the supplied technical-audit, keyword and Google Ads visuals and keyword PDF are included with their actual dates. Historical visuals below are labelled by month and are not October results. Booking-import and double-counting verification remain pending.

visuals.caption: October 2026 reporting — technical audit crawled November 1, 2026

recap: The supplied Ubersuggest audit, crawled November 1, 2026 at 10:27 PM (tool-displayed time), is a dated follow-up for October. It shows an on-page SEO score of 100 and two remaining issues: two pages with poorly formatted URLs. It does not establish an issue-free site.

The audit lists 205 page entries: 144 crawled and 61 blocked. Of the crawled pages, 131 were successful, 13 redirected and none broken. Its snapshot also reports estimated organic monthly traffic of 306, 292 organic keywords and 263 backlinks. These are Ubersuggest snapshot metrics, not verified October Analytics/Search Console totals or counts of newly built links. The backlink snapshot is separate from Leanne’s earlier 180-to-201 monitoring period.

On October 30, 25 unique French meta descriptions were published, and all 50 URLs from the duplicate-description audit were verified live. No duplicate descriptions remained within that audited set. The 50-URL verification was separate from the newly supplied November 1 crawl.

French headings, navigation and body translations still need work. A subsequent check confirmed the metadata fixes were already live; it did not represent another 25 edits. Review the two URL-format issues from the new crawl. An October technical-audit PDF has not been supplied.

visuals.caption: October 2026 reporting — Google Ads snapshot October 5–November 1, 2026

recap: Google Ads management was added to Shift’s services in October, alongside ongoing SEO and content work. October 20–26 work included a dedicated Pelvic Health landing-page design and conversion-focused copy. Advertising wording was reviewed against the client’s feedback; final compliant copy, approval and development remain outstanding.

The supplied Google Ads screenshot covers October 5–November 1, 2026, not the full calendar month of October. It reports 125 clicks, 2.67K impressions, 10.00 conversions and a displayed cost of $2.06K. The currency is not identified in this screenshot and remains unverified. These aggregate conversions are not confirmed unique appointments or patients; they must not be equated with the action-level All conversions baseline below.
Campaign, search-term, targeting, schedule and budget reviews remain next steps; proposed optimizations are not presented as completed changes. No matched-period performance comparison is asserted.
googleAds.reportHtml:
November 1, 2026 — conversion validation follow-up

This post-period update is separate from October performance. The Google Ads, GTM and GA4 setup, conversion linker, click and lead-form triggers, and active campaign landing pages were reviewed. No campaigns, budgets, conversion goals, tags or settings were changed, and no GTM version was published.

Observed click test — passed

Book Online on the Physiotherapy page opened Jane. The Google Ads Jane click tag succeeded once and the GA4 Jane click tag fired once; GA4 Realtime recorded click_jane_tm = 1. This verifies the observed outbound click, not an Ads-attributed conversion or completed appointment. A phone-click event was observed, but full call attribution and email/form end-to-end tests remain unverified.

Genuine booking — confirmed; Ads import pending

A legitimate appointment was booked through Jane on November 1 and a confirmation email arrived. Appointment details are omitted. No completion debug trace was captured. At the subsequent check, October 31 was still the latest visible upload; no correlated new booking upload was visible.

Before-and-after checks — pending

The baseline covers October 5–November 1, 2026, not the full October reporting period. Values below are reported conversion values; currency is unverified.

Conversion actionBefore: All conversionsReported valueConfiguration / statusAfter
Janeapp Click210Active; Primary; Count OnePending
Jane Online Booking61,080Needs attention; Primary; Count EveryPending

Nine records in the visible October 22–31 import entries failed, with 0% success across those entries. Earlier entries included successes. Exact rejection reasons are unknown; duplicate rejection has not been established.

Double-counting checks remain pending. Janeapp Click and Jane Online Booking are both Primary account-default goals, so click-plus-booking overlap may affect aggregate reporting. This is separate from duplicate tag firing. A separate Jane container was detected, but its configuration was not verified; multiple containers alone do not prove duplication. Aggregate conversions must not be treated as unique bookings or patients.

Next, compare the same actions and date range after processing; correlate the genuine booking with its confirmation time and booking identifier; confirm timezone, attribution eligibility and reporting latency; inspect exact upload errors and retry deduplication with the integration owner or Jane support. A totals increase alone cannot prove attribution or absence of duplicates. No repeat appointment is needed. Booking-import reliability and absence of double counting remain unverified.
